runners_data.name: Etienne
runners_data.comment: A February foal by Rajasinghe whose brother was very useful over 6f, and the dam was effective at 7f; Etienne has never run and the record of the yard on debut is a factor — respect is due if the market signals support, though he goes entirely on breeding and reputation from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Good Fighter
runners_data.comment: Outpaced throughout on debut at Windsor and beaten 6¼l, with the longer trip today expected to be more suitable; Good Fighter has a trainer in good form and handles today's conditions — too far behind on debut to inspire confidence but the step up in trip could bring out more from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Jackson Canyon
runners_data.comment: A $105,000 son of Jack Christopher whose dam was a useful US dirt performer over 5f; Jackson Canyon is unraced but comes from a strong Irish yard and the market will be telling — well worth considering on debut from stall 2 if supported, and the pedigree suggests the trip will be within range.

runners_data.name: Lion Of God
runners_data.comment: A 75,000gns breeze-up purchase by Invincible Spirit, with a half-brother who showed smart form at 8f and a dam that stayed 10f; Lion Of God has never run and may find this a learning run on debut, though the pedigree is interesting from stall 5 and the yard will have him ready to show something.

runners_data.name: Mysterious Times
runners_data.comment: Third on debut at Sandown, showing a fair amount while a touch free early, and the yard has a fine recent record at this meeting with its juveniles; Mysterious Times handles this course and the going, and a top trainer-jockey combination who have a strong record here points to further progress from stall 1 now stepped up to 6f.

runners_data.name: Weekend Roar
runners_data.comment: Third beaten 1¼l on debut at Salisbury and handles this course and going; Weekend Roar hinted at genuine ability on debut, is proven at this trip, and Oisin Murphy takes the ride — yet to win but the debut form is solid and improvement looks likely, with the main query being whether the step up in class catches him out from stall 4.

races.name: Lay & Wheeler Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Areti
runners_data.comment: Placed consistently on good-to-soft and AW before a below-par run back on soft turf at Salisbury last time; Areti is without a win in recent starts but drier conditions today are more in her favour, and first-time tongue-tie and headgear could unlock improvement — that said, more is needed from stall 6 to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Esdaile
runners_data.comment: An improvement on her first run when upped to 1m at Yarmouth, beaten 5½l but keeping on into sixth; Esdaile handles today's trip and is clearly developing, though winless in two starts and ranked lowest in the field, she needs a further step forward from stall 2 to be a factor.

runners_data.name: Siddal
runners_data.comment: Surprised at huge odds when finishing a narrow second at Salisbury, finishing with real purpose in the closing stages and clear of the remainder; Siddal is yet to win but showed there is real ability there when conditions suit — soft ground is her forte and today's sounder surface poses a genuine question from stall 5, making improvement less certain.

runners_data.name: Vanilla Skies
runners_data.comment: A daughter of Pinatubo whose dam was useful at 7f, and her half-sister to Brewing brings smart 7f form into the pedigree; Vanilla Skies is blinkered on debut for a well-regarded yard and warrants serious consideration if the market takes an interest — unraced, so entirely on trust from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Shamalza
runners_data.comment: Connections were successful in this contest twelve months ago and the stable retains potential here; Shamalza handled the trip last time but never really threatened and was held with ease, and while she acts on good ground and there is ability to uncover, the figures place her behind the top two in this field from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Afraj
runners_data.comment: Took a maiden at Chelmsford on debut and then shaped with promise upped sharply in trip at Goodwood, keeping on into third; Afraj handles 7f to 1m and acts on good-to-soft and AW, with the drop back in distance likely to help if she settles — a jockey with a fine record at this course and a trainer firing at 29% in the past fortnight make her the one to side with from stall 4.

races.name: Hallgarten Wines Jockey Club Partner Handicap

runners_data.name: Change Sings
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground performer at 6f with a 1W3P record in similar conditions, sits naturally prominent and benefits maximally from Angel Gabriel's controlled lead; Eve Johnson Houghton's 6/32 recent trainer strike rate is moderate but the horse's own course-and-distance profile is the real selling point here.
runners_data.comment: Beaten off this mark at Windsor in recent outings and a return to form is needed; Change Sings does enjoy making the running, which at least gives her something to aim for, and she handles 5f to 7f on a range of going — from stall 8 she can press on, but winless in recent starts means she requires a big step up.

runners_data.name: Sixtygeesbaby
runners_data.note: Hold-up style under the accomplished D Tudhope, returning after 40 days off with tongue tie — the fresher profile may have sharpened him but he needs a stronger gallop than this race is likely to produce to get competitive; sim-going record of 9/11 with 2W4P suggests the surface is no issue.
runners_data.comment: Came from off the pace and was well short of her best after a difficult start at Newmarket last time; Sixtygeesbaby handles 6f to 7f on a sound surface and first-time tongue-tie is applied today — still without a handicap success and needing to prove more from stall 6, she is hard to trust at this stage.

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: Sharp recent form including a win and multiple places at 6f on Good, but this naturally prominent type is likely to find himself racing out of his preferred position as Angel Gabriel and Change Sings fill the front slots — that positional compromise tempers confidence despite strong raw figures.
runners_data.comment: Third last time off a mark of 73, beaten 4l, and returns just 2lb higher at a course and distance he handles; Fiscal Policy has come back into form recently and stays effective at 6f on fast ground and AW — the in-form trainer stat is a mild negative but the overall profile from stall 7 makes him a live contender.

runners_data.name: Angel Gabriel
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Rossa Ryan and R M Beckett returning after a lengthy 192-day absence; his OR of 82 and prior form (two seconds and a win) shows quality, but the layoff is a notable unknown and his ability to sustain his effort over the full 6f after such a break is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Given a clear run to the front at Lingfield last time, the gelding settled matters smoothly to take a novice by 1¼l and looks to have come on for that; Angel Gabriel handles 6f well and the profile looks solid for a handicap debut — 192 days away is the one query from stall 1, but connections' confidence makes him hard to overlook.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sands
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature but pushed into a midfield mapping here because the race has no room for him up front — Ryan Moore is the class jockey upgrade and his 1W2P sim-going record is acceptable, but racing out of his preferred position on this straight track is a real tactical disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Third at Hamilton beaten 3l at a trip shorter than today's, suggesting the return to 6f or 7f is a positive; Sierra Sands handles today's conditions well and tops our ratings in this field — consistent around these marks and capable on the form, with stall 4 neutral; the chief concern is the early pace.

runners_data.name: Fresh Fade
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for the small-yard Attwater stable (T14: 1/11), recent form is patchy (0-4-5-6-0-4-5) and his sim-going record of 11/13 with limited wins suggests he needs things to go perfectly — a fast pace that doesn't materialise makes his task harder.
runners_data.comment: Form has fallen away in recent starts and beaten well down the field at Windsor last time; Fresh Fade handles the trip and going but is ranked lowest on our figures and her current trajectory makes it hard to see her reversing things from stall 2, with the form a real concern at this stage.

runners_data.name: Ice Cube
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse that the mapping has placed in midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — racing at OR 61 in a field rated up to 82, the class differential is stark, and Saffie Osborne will need everything to fall right; his best efforts have come over further (8f) and this 6f on Good looks tight for his style.
runners_data.comment: Beaten down the field at Goodwood off a longer trip, and seems better suited back at 7f to 8f; Ice Cube gets first-time blinkers today and the trainer is in good form — without a win in recent starts, but the headgear could sharpen the picture and the official rating of 61 leaves a degree of upside from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Secret History
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 6f and 7f on Flat going, now with Oisin Murphy in the saddle — a significant booking — and a sim-going record of 4/5 with 1W3P confirms course-going suitability; racing from a prominent position just off the pace is exactly the profile this race shape appears set to reward.

races.paceDynamic: Angel Gabriel is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to press him hard from the off, he should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over the straight six at Newmarket rather than a lung-bursting, unsustainable bolt. Change Sings and Secret History will look to sit just off the pace in the prominent positions, giving them first run on any who hold back. This field contains more naturally prominent horses than the race shape can accommodate — Sierra Sands and Fiscal Policy are genuine pace-seeking types but are most likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield as Angel Gabriel and Change Sings fill the early slots, which meaningfully compromises their chances. A steady-to-honest pace set by a single front-runner on Good ground at Newmarket — a course that consistently rewards horses travelling prominently and quickening in the final two furlongs — tilts the tactical verdict firmly toward horses racing in the first three, particularly those who can sit just off Angel Gabriel and pounce when he comes off the bridle inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Angel Gabriel Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Gabriel sets a controlled, uncontested gallop and the race is run at an honest but not brutal tempo, allowing horses just off the pace to pounce.
scenarios.body: If Angel Gabriel sets a controlled, uncontested gallop and the race is run at an honest but not brutal tempo, allowing horses just off the pace to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Angel Gabriel Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Gabriel is allowed to build such a comfortable lead through the early stages that he finds a second wind and holds every challenge.
scenarios.body: If Angel Gabriel is allowed to build such a comfortable lead through the early stages that he finds a second wind and holds every challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is significantly faster than expected, causing the prominent horses to tie up and leaving the hold-up runners with a gap to exploit in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is significantly faster than expected, causing the prominent horses to tie up and leaving the hold-up runners with a gap to exploit in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Gabriel goes off too fast and collapses dramatically inside the final furlong, gifting the race to horses who were shuffled into midfield.
scenarios.body: If Angel Gabriel goes off too fast and collapses dramatically inside the final furlong, gifting the race to horses who were shuffled into midfield.

watchPoints.text: Angel Gabriel's 192-day absence is the single biggest risk factor in this race — watch the market move closely, and if he drifts sharply pre-race his fitness may be in doubt, which would collapse the dominant pace scenario entirely.

Sierra Sands and Fiscal Policy — both naturally prominent types — will be jostling for a position they cannot both hold; watch the early stalls for a scrimmage that could compromise one or both and benefit Change Sings who has a cleaner draw on the rail side.

Sixtygeesbaby is 40 days off the track with tongue tie, and D Tudhope's booking adds interest — if he comes forward in the market from his current starting point it may indicate stable confidence that the freshener has him cherry-ripe.

Secret History's Oisin Murphy booking stands out as the highest-profile jockey engagement in the field; watch whether Murphy elects to track Angel Gabriel from the front or lets him go and sits third or fourth, as that positioning choice will be telling.

Good ground is consistent across all morning readings at Newmarket — no unexpected softening that might reshuffle going preferences — so all OK-tagged runners can be taken at face value and no going-related market moves should be expected.

races.name: Empress Fillies' Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Beauty Box
runners_data.note: Good-ground specialist (3 from 3 on similar going) trained by J Tate, she has won over this 6f trip and her recent form of 421 shows progressive improvement; her style is uncertain but the Good conditions and trainer's decent 14-day strike rate give her each-way claims off a low OR.
runners_data.comment: Winning form at this trip and on this ground stands up, and a 2l success at Ripon last time out was straightforward enough; the step up in grade is the question now for Beauty Box, and she will need to build on that to feature from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Californian Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly by Cieren Fallon and H Palmer (strong 6/32 T14), sole run was a solid third over this exact 6f/Good combination; should sit last or second-last before a late challenge, making her a prime beneficiary if the contested early pace softens up the leaders.
runners_data.comment: Debut third beaten 2½l at Nottingham showed there is ability there, and this trip on a sound surface suits; yet to win and the sharp grade rise makes Californian Angel tough to fancy from stall 7, though the form base gives her a platform to improve.

runners_data.name: Glorious Game
runners_data.note: Top-rated joint favourite (OR=120) for H Palmer who will look to roll along from the front under Oisin Murphy; her only run was on Soft, which is a surface query on Good ground today, and tongue-tie is noted as headgear — Murphy's tactical nous is the key variable in how aggressively she contests the lead.
runners_data.comment: Debut scorer at Windsor, finding extra to assert by 1½l, and the finish suggested there is more to come; Glorious Game looks useful and the first-time tongue-tie is worth noting, though the step into a higher grade from stall 8 now tests how good she really is.

runners_data.name: Havana Sprite
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has raced three times on Good ground and knows how to bowl along; trained by J Tate alongside Beauty Box, she must overcome a big OR deficit against the three 120-rated rivals, and her best hope is stealing a march before the class horses catch her.
runners_data.comment: Landed a novice at Bath by 2½l last time with plenty in hand, and this trip should be within her compass on a surface she handles; Havana Sprite tops our ratings and looks the one to beat, with a step up in grade the only caveat after just three recent outings.

runners_data.name: Margaret's Pearl
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-piece and has been given 41 days since last run, which demands attention; her single win came over 5f so stepping to 6f on Good is an open question, and her recent form figures of 410 — including a blank — make her hard to trust at this level from a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Overwhelmed by the pace and well held in a Listed race at York last time, though that came after a win the previous start; cheekpieces go on for the first time. Margaret's Pearl handles today's trip and ground but sits bottom of our ratings and will need others to underperform from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Motown Filly
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose only run was a second on Soft, ridden by Saffie Osborne for R Spencer (T14: 7/18 — active yard); she is stepping up to Good ground with just the one run on her card, so there is a degree of unknown about her ground preference, but her OR=120 marks her as fully competitive.
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye on debut at Windsor, finishing strongly to be beaten only 1½l in second, and the trainer is in good form; Motown Filly is yet to win but has the ability and this trip on good-to-soft suits her well — the jump in grade is the main test from stall 5.

runners_data.name: The Can Can Queen
runners_data.note: Prominent-running filly for C Johnston (large yard, 5/45 T14) who has won over 6f on Good ground — the key positive — and PJ McDonald's experience is an asset; form figures of 515 include a win and a couple of moderate efforts so she is consistent without being dominant.
runners_data.comment: Came up short when dropped back in trip at Beverley last time, finding the shorter trip too sharp when beaten 5l, but returns to 6f today which is her best distance on good ground; The Can Can Queen has won at this level and is capable of running well, though in-and-out form from stall 4 means she cannot be relied upon.

runners_data.name: What A Girl Wants
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly (form 3220, Good-ground profile) trained by K P De Foy with only a 1/19 T14 rate; she ran just six days ago which is worth monitoring for freshness, and her recent run-outs over 6f on Good show she handles the conditions, but her record of places without a win raises questions about a finishing kick at Listed level.
runners_data.comment: Listed-placed form in Ireland set a high standard before a tough Group 3 on stable debut left her beaten; in good shape beforehand and acts on soft as well as today's ground, What A Girl Wants is a filly of real quality whose best efforts demand respect — just needs to recapture that earlier level from stall 6.

races.paceDynamic: Glorious Game and Havana Sprite are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the outset over this 6f Newmarket straight, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft, uncontested lead for either. Glorious Game (Oisin Murphy, OR=120) brings the higher class but has only run on Soft, while Havana Sprite (Hector Crouch, OR=85) has three Good-ground runs and may press harder than her OR suggests. The duel between them should produce an honest, even pace that ensures the race is truly run — no crawl, no false tempo — with two furlongs of genuine racing left. This shape favours prominent racers and midfield closers who can track a legitimate gallop and sustain their effort into the Rowley Mile dip, rather than hold-up types who need something to fall apart at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Glorious Game and Havana Sprite push each other hard enough to leave them both vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Glorious Game and Havana Sprite push each other hard enough to leave them both vulnerable in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Glorious Game Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Glorious Game settles in a rhythm rather than battling and asserts class from the front against inferior OR rivals.
scenarios.body: If Glorious Game settles in a rhythm rather than battling and asserts class from the front against inferior OR rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Havana Sprite Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Sprite quickens first from Glorious Game early and Glorious Game fails to match her, leaving Havana Sprite in an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: If Havana Sprite quickens first from Glorious Game early and Glorious Game fails to match her, leaving Havana Sprite in an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running duel collapses with all principals stopping, opening the race for hold-up horses to plunder.
scenarios.body: If the front-running duel collapses with all principals stopping, opening the race for hold-up horses to plunder.

watchPoints.text: Glorious Game and Havana Sprite — watch the first furlong closely to see who blinks first; if both commit to an all-out duel the contest will be set up for hold-up and midfield horses to finish strongly, fundamentally altering the likely winner profile.

Californian Angel — Cieren Fallon is likely to settle her at the back, so watch her position at the halfway point; if she is still further back than midfield with two furlongs to run on this straight, she may simply not have enough track to deliver her challenge.

Glorious Game (sole run on Soft) — the Going Report confirms a Good surface all day; if she is a notably better horse on easier ground, her contested front-running role becomes more physically demanding than it would be on her preferred surface.

Margaret's Pearl — 41 days off the track combined with headgear (tongue-piece) and a step up to 6f makes her an interesting betting proposition; if she jumps and goes prominent she could outrun her OR, but if she misses the break the trip from the rear at Listed level is a tough ask.

What A Girl Wants — ran only six days ago and returns quickly for K P De Foy; watch her in the paddock for any signs of a below-par preparation, as a hold-up filly who needs everything to go right cannot afford to be less than 100% sharp.

races.name: laywheeler.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Superposition
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a win and a place from two starts on Good going at 7f; trips to Haydock over 8f have not suited but returning to this course/distance profile is a positive, and Jack Callan's booking for Ed Dunlop's yard is straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Came from off the pace and really knuckled down to take a handicap at Newmarket by a neck last time, and the track and conditions suit again; Superposition is three pounds higher here and an inconsistent profile means this is not a certainty, but he has the class to run up to his best again from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Dark Tornado
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse wearing a visor, with all five recent runs on Good and a solid finishing record, though he has not won in 12 attempts on this going — the style suits a hot pace but the winning thread is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Blocked for room late at Newmarket last time and likely left with more to offer than the margin shows, beaten 3½l off this mark; Dark Tornado acts on a sound surface at this trip but has been well held in recent starts, and the visor goes on for the first time — the in-form trainer is a mild positive, yet he remains hard to trust from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Darkness
runners_data.note: A consistent visor-wearer who races from well off the pace; eight-year-old with solid Good-ground credentials over 7f at Newmarket specifically, but a finishing position of 11th last time out here is a caution, and David O'Meara's yard has been busy.
runners_data.comment: Trailed in rear when well held off the pace at York last time, beaten 6l in a handicap; Darkness wears the visor for the first time today and clearly handles today's trip and conditions, but has been beaten out of sight in recent runs and needs more than headgear to turn it around from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: Has an OR of 89 and placed twice recently; a natural hold-up operator whose true racing position will be further back than the map suggests — he will need more pace than Northern Express alone is likely to generate, which tempers his chances despite Appleby's 14-day record of 2/17 being modest.
runners_data.comment: Freshened up since a runner-up effort at Newbury two runs back, and has placed form in the grade; Nostrum handles today's trip and any ground, and cheekpieces go on for the first time, though he is no longer the force of old and the trainer's recent strike rate gives little confidence from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Philanthropist
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good going (1/7f/GOO) and is a confirmed prominent racer by nature; the field is too deep in similar types for him to secure his preferred early slot, which means Rossa Ryan will need to be patient from a position that doesn't fully suit.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time off a mark of 85, beaten 2½l, and returns off the same rating today; first-time headgear is a positive for Philanthropist, and he handles these conditions well over 7f to 8f — strong pace brings out his best, and the main uncertainty from stall 3 is whether conditions fire him on the day.

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride on a horse whose natural instinct is to race from the rear, but five of his last six placings on Good turf have come from 7th position or further back — the concern is that the pace generated today may not be extreme enough to bring him into it from where he will actually be.
runners_data.comment: Has excuses for his York run, beaten 7¼l but not himself that day, and now 3lb below his last winning mark; Aalto usually comes from off the pace and handles today's trip and surface well, and a level-headed trainer booking in Ryan Moore points to confidence — inconsistency is the caveat, but the ratings put him marginally ahead from stall 1.

runners_data.name: I Still Have Faith
runners_data.note: De Sousa partners a horse who has placed twice at 8f on Good but shapes as a true prominent type unable to get to the front in this traffic; the tongue-tie worn previously is not listed here, and the trainer's 14-day record of 0/17 is a live caution.
runners_data.comment: Beaten out of the places last time at Newbury after solid form prior, and effective over 7f to 10f on any going; first-time tongue-tie could help I Still Have Faith from stall 11, though she is winless in recent starts and needs to bounce back sharply — she has the profile to do so but is hard to rely on.

runners_data.name: Silver Ghost
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon partners a lightly-raced four-year-old with an excellent course record — 2W7P from 13 runs on Good, all at 7f at Newmarket — and his two placed runs here this year confirm he handles this track and this ground exceptionally well.

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning from a 126-day break for Michael Dods, who has a 14-day record of 2/8 — the fitness query after such a layoff is real, though horses trained to lead can go fresh; his OR of 96 is the highest in the field, and Sean Kirrane will need to use him from the outset.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a four-month break after a useful display beaten 5l at Bahrain, and effective over today's trip and ground; first-time headgear could sharpen Northern Express, though he has been winless in recent starts and faces stronger opposition from stall 10 off OR 96.

runners_data.name: Mudbir
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on a four-year-old with consecutive wins (7f/Good, 7f/Soft) before a fifth-place finish at 8f; has only four runs on Good at 7f with one win and one placing, and the Gosden yard's 14-day record of 7/36 is in line with expectations — a prominent horse with tactical speed if Buick can get him into position.
runners_data.comment: Won twice last season and was progressive before meeting trouble on his reappearance, unable to quicken when down the field at Ascot; with the gelding operation behind him and conditions that suit, Mudbir has the tools to bounce back from stall 2, though a 47-day break and first-time headgear bring a question mark.

runners_data.name: Hawksbill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from a 111-day absence for Richard Spencer, who is in good form (T14: 7/18); all recent runs have been on Good going and his best efforts were at 7f, but the fitness question after nearly four months off and a tendency to finish mid-pack limits confidence despite a suitable race shape if the pace is fast.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a lengthy break off a mark that now looks fair for this grade, and effective over 7f to 1m on a sound surface; Hawksbill held his own against stronger company last time and is able to compete off this rating — the main risk from stall 8 is whether the break dulls his edge.

races.paceDynamic: Northern Express is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with a clear lead rôle unchallenged, shapes to set a measured, sustainable gallop over this 7f Rowley Mile trip on Good ground — a tempo that will not stretch the field excessively but will create a genuine test for closers who need a strong pace to finish through. Silver Ghost, Superposition, and Mudbir are all genuine prominent types and will press for early position behind Northern Express, meaning the first two or three furlongs will see a competitive scramble for the first three slots before the pace settles. This field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Philanthropist and I Still Have Faith are true prominent racers who will be unable to secure their natural ground and will effectively race in a compromised midfield position, while Nostrum and Aalto are genuine hold-up horses similarly displaced toward midfield on the map. The dominant race shape — a steady-to-fair pace set by Northern Express with a prominent group tracking close — strongly favours horses who can race just off the leader in the first three or four, as the Rowley Mile's straight run-in rewards those with tactical position and the ability to quicken on Good ground rather than deep closers needing a true end-to-end gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Northern Express Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express crosses cleanly and dictates an uncontested, honest-but-not-scorching pace, the race is run entirely to suit horses racing in the first three.
scenarios.body: If Northern Express crosses cleanly and dictates an uncontested, honest-but-not-scorching pace, the race is run entirely to suit horses racing in the first three.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack instinctively backs off Northern Express early, the front-runner is allowed an uncontested and artificially slow early gallop that turns the race into a stamina-sapping sprint from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If the prominent pack instinctively backs off Northern Express early, the front-runner is allowed an uncontested and artificially slow early gallop that turns the race into a stamina-sapping sprint from 2f out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pressure Builds, Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mudbir or Silver Ghost push Northern Express for the lead from the off, the pace becomes genuinely hot and the race plays into the hands of hold-up horses who can pick up a strong gallop.
scenarios.body: If Mudbir or Silver Ghost push Northern Express for the lead from the off, the pace becomes genuinely hot and the race plays into the hands of hold-up horses who can pick up a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just right — honest without being brutal — and the prominent group is slightly crowded entering the Dip, a horse threading from midfield with a well-timed gap can emerge late.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just right — honest without being brutal — and the prominent group is slightly crowded entering the Dip, a horse threading from midfield with a well-timed gap can emerge late.

watchPoints.text: Northern Express's 126-day absence is the race's single biggest variable — if he shows any signs of freshness or greenness in the opening furlong, the pace scenario collapses and the entire shape pivots.

Monitor the early stalls draw and the first-furlong positioning battle: Silver Ghost, Mudbir, and Superposition are all prominent types who will contest the same ground behind Northern Express, and any bump or crowding could redistribute the race shape dramatically before the pace settles.

Philanthropist and I Still Have Faith — both natural prominent types — will be squeezed into a midfield role against their instincts; if either over-races or uses energy chasing their preferred position, their finishing kick will be compromised.

Dark Tornado has run 12 times on Good ground without winning — if the pace is only fair rather than strong, his hold-up style is unlikely to generate sufficient momentum for a winning run despite his consistent placed form.

Hawksbill's 111-day layoff for a trainer who fires fresh horses (7/18 over 14 days) is worth monitoring in the market — if confidence builds around Spencer's horses' fitness coming off a break, that represents a live situational angle in this shape.

races.name: hnwines.co.uk Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Crystal Pier
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance last time and steps back in having been up to 10f; Rossa Ryan is a strong booking for Beckett and her hold-up style is best served when there is enough pace ahead to close into — this tempo may just be sufficient.|
runners_data.comment: Narrow runner-up off a mark of 75 last time shows she is right in the mix at this level; Crystal Pier is effective from 7f to 9f on a sound surface and is able to compete at this level — the 4lb rise from that run is the only concern from stall 2, and she has the profile to be very competitive.

runners_data.name: Darzah
runners_data.note: Haggas filly with a win on Fibresand and two efforts on Good turf showing inconsistency; Cieren Fallon picks her up and she is naturally prominent enough to sit a comfortable second or third behind Silent City without expending early energy.|
runners_data.comment: Won two runs back and has experience of this trip and going, with the surface suiting; below form when beaten 6l in a handicap at Sandown last time, but effective at a mile on a sound surface and a return to form looks likely — Darzah tops our ratings and the form points her out as the one to beat, with stall 3 a fine draw.

runners_data.name: Luna Celeste
runners_data.note: Dropped back from 6f sprint form to a mile is the key question here for Tom Clover's filly; she showed good placed form at 6f on Tapeta but Saffie Osborne's strong early positioning could see her slot in just behind Silent City and produce her best if the extra two furlongs suit.|
runners_data.comment: Secured a narrow maiden success at Leicester last time, keeping on gamely to get up in a short-head finish, and the form is encouraging; Luna Celeste is now stepping up 2f in trip for the first time, which is the main question from stall 4, but on good-to-firm and AW form she has scope to handle it if settlement is no issue.

runners_data.name: Come On Eibhlin
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's filly is a genuine hold-up operator by style but with several prominent types in the field she will struggle to find clear cover at the rear — her true role is closer than the map can place her, so discount her unless the pace genuinely collapses in the straight.|
runners_data.comment: Placed at Wetherby in her last outing beaten only ¾l off a 1lb higher mark, and handles this trip on a sound surface; Come On Eibhlin is versatile from 5f to 8f and acts on reasonable ground — she is winless in recent starts but the form shows she goes close, and from stall 5 she is capable of running another sound race, though stronger rivals set the bar higher.

runners_data.name: Thursday Girl
runners_data.note: Listed as non-runner — no tactical assessment applicable; her form of placed efforts at 7f on Good and Tapeta suggested she would have been a prominent factor, but she does not run.|

runners_data.name: Silent City
runners_data.note: Varian's filly boasts two wins and two places from five course-and-distance efforts on Good, making her form profile highly relevant, but 246 days off is a significant fitness flag — if she is cherry-ripe she controls this; if not, she may lack the sharpness to dictate cleanly, and STYLE_FIT suggests her position at the head may be more vulnerable than her OR of 82 implies.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts with two wins in five outings, and runner-up off a mark only 2lb lower at Newmarket last time; Silent City has been off the track for 246 days and returns on a good mark with a handler in good recent form — the break is the only real concern from stall 1, and this remains a strong profile.

runners_data.name: Bridget's View
runners_data.note: A four-year-old beaten in seven of seven career runs with form figures showing she has never gone close on Good turf at 7-8f; the 7lb claim from Olivia Haines for S C Williams helps the weight, but the raw form offers nothing to recommend her and she needs a significant step up in form to feature.|
runners_data.comment: Plodding in recent outings with three consecutive placed finishes below seventh, and yet to win in recent starts; Bridget's View handles this trip and ground but has been winless and her mark keeps easing — there is ability there over 7f to 8f on good-to-soft, but more is needed from stall 6 before she can be seriously fancied.

races.paceDynamic: Silent City is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with a long absence of 246 days to shake off, is likely to bowl along at a measured, self-regulated tempo rather than a scorching gallop — creating a sustainable, single-file procession around the Rowley Mile. Darzah and Luna Celeste will press forward from stalls, but neither has the natural desire to challenge for the lead, meaning Silent City should dictate unopposed on a flat course that rewards horses who settle well off honest fractions. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race can comfortably accommodate — Come On Eibhlin is a genuine hold-up performer pushed into a midfield mapping and is unlikely to find the deep cover she needs. A controlled, even-tempo mile on Good ground at Newmarket with no genuine pace pressure overwhelmingly favours a prominent racer or a horse travelling sweetly just off the leader who can quicken from a handy position — deep closers launching from the back will find the sectionals insufficient to bridge the gap.

watchPoints.text: Silent City's 246-day absence is the single biggest variable — watch her in the paddock and early strides for signs she is short of peak fitness, which would immediately open the race to Darzah and Luna Celeste.

Come On Eibhlin is a true hold-up horse who cannot naturally access her preferred deep position in this seven-runner field — if D Egan is forced wide or forward early, her finishing effort will be significantly compromised.

Luna Celeste has all her best form at 6f and steps up two furlongs here; if she does not settle behind Silent City in the early stages and races too freely, her stamina may give out before the final furlong.

Crystal Pier has won and placed over course and distance on Good ground — she is the one hold-up horse whose profile genuinely fits a Newmarket mile if Silent City does go off too quickly and creates a pace she can close into.

Thursday Girl is a non-runner, reducing the field to six effective runners and removing one prominent-type from the race shape, which slightly increases the chances of Silent City finding a completely uncontested lead.
